title: Research Journal #39 -- What We Found When We Completed the macOS Stress Tests
html:
Research Journal #38 documented the macOS and Windows portability checks that established a defined baseline for BTLB-SIM. The Architecture Stress Audit then challenged that baseline under adverse conditions to see where its guarantees held and where they needed closer examination.

On the evening of September 21, 2026, we could account for every case in the BTLB-SIM Architecture Stress Audit on macOS. The ledger had 30 rows. Twenty-two passed the local checks that had been exercised, and eight recorded failures. Every row still awaited native Windows execution.

Case dispositions at the September 21, 2026 checkpoint
Disposition macOS Combined
PASS 22 0
FAIL 8 8
INCONCLUSIVE 0 22
Total 30 30

All 30 cases were pending native Windows execution at this checkpoint, including the eight already recorded as combined failures.

Research Journal Entry 17 described the first six findings. The expanded run added two more. Both came from asking how far a verification check actually reaches.

When a record exists in two places (AR17-009)

One test examined a record represented in two places. The larger record carried an intact embedded copy. A separately stored row held another copy. We corrupted that separate row in a disposable test fixture and asked the verifier to check the larger record. The check accepted it. A repeat produced the same outcome.

That exposed a question the architecture would have to settle. When the verifier checks a record, which stored representations does its guarantee cover? The observation establishes what the check accepted in this setup. The obligation to validate both representations still required review. [1, 2]

When the inventory changes after startup (AR17-012)

The second test changed the inventory used to verify an execution release. The control rejected a change made before the engine was constructed. In the tested configuration, a change made after construction was accepted, and the behavior was repeated.

The timing matters. A check performed during construction can establish what the engine saw at that point. The later result raises a separate question about how long that assurance holds. The audit recorded a release-identity problem under the exercised conditions. Whether it affected any numerical result was outside the test. [1, 2]

Why the Windows column stayed open

The ledger could record a failure as soon as the audit observed it on macOS. Giving a case a combined-platform pass required evidence from both platforms. At this checkpoint, the combined ledger therefore held eight observed failures and 22 inconclusive cases. The Windows package was ready, and its local smoke checks helped verify the package. Native Windows execution was still the next step. [1]

The boundary checks also recorded that all 683 tracked baseline files matched their expected hashes. The existing VAPE and WC archive verifiers passed their scoped checks. Those records give us a way to identify the baseline and the archived material examined during discovery. [1, 3]

Research status at this checkpoint

AR-1.7 discovery remained open. The findings were internal software observations, with no production correction or architecture acceptance at this stage. The work produced no new physics simulation result, independent scientific reproduction, or physical experimental evidence. The next question was whether the native Windows run would confirm the observed behaviors and exercise the coverage that macOS could not supply.

Sources

The RJ39 supporting-evidence package contains the 30-case disposition ledger, excerpts from the original observations and controls, the archive-verifier outputs, and a manifest and checksums. Start with README.md.

The package includes selected excerpts from original internal records so readers can examine the documented findings and controls. Complete executable reproduction would require the full harness, fixtures, and source and archive materials. The recorded repeats were internal, and independent reproduction remains unestablished.

  1. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Discovery Summary — local boundary, native Windows pending, v2, and its 30-case disposition ledger. Audit specification 51e6d4cfe1e5b906b0691df006205160a4184f5d, acceptance baseline 2e3af1d33012c15110d470f3619eafc5ecf2f982.
  2. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Failure Observation Register, v2. Case 009 observations AR17-OBS-0033 and AR17-OBS-0034. Case 012 observations AR17-OBS-0039 and AR17-OBS-0040.
  3. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Boundary Integrity, v2, and case AR17-030, attempt 004. Baseline-file inventory and VAPE and WC archive-verifier outputs.
